servers.description: Edge Delivery Services (EDS) Admin API client — CLI and MCP server.

env.name: EDS_ORG
env.description: The Edge Delivery Services organisation every eds_* tool addresses. The server resolves it on the first tool call and refuses the call without it; tools/list still works.

env.name: EDS_TOKEN
env.description: Admin API bearer. Every tool call needs one, but it may come from this variable OR from the credential file written by `hiberus-eds auth token set`, so neither source is required on its own.

env.name: EDS_SITE
env.description: Default site for `hiberus-eds` CLI commands that take one. Read by the CLI only — the MCP server never reads it, and a site is passed per tool call instead.

tools.name: eds_get_status
tools.description: Use this when you need one path's current status across edit/preview/live/code/index on a single site — the smallest, cheapest status call.

tools.name: eds_get_status_bulk
tools.description: Use this when you need status for several paths on a site at once instead of calling eds_get_status in a loop.

tools.name: eds_set_live_state
tools.description: Use this to publish or unpublish one or more paths on a site. Destructive: it changes what is publicly live.
tools.unverified: Never run against a live Edge Delivery Services site. The Admin API publishes content that already exists rather than creating it; the site this package was developed against keeps its content in AEM as a Cloud Service, and the package ships no preview operation, so there was no page that could be published safely. Its request shape is covered by unit tests and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: eds_get_site_config
tools.description: Use this when you need a site's full effective configuration — the site document alone does not resolve inheritance.

tools.name: eds_reindex
tools.description: Use this to re-run indexing for specific paths, or — only with explicit double confirmation — the entire site.
tools.unverified: Never run against a live Edge Delivery Services site, at either scope.

tools.name: eds_get_audit_log
tools.description: Use this to review recent changes to a site. Returns one page of entries plus a nextToken cursor.

tools.name: eds_get_snapshots
tools.description: Use this to list a site's snapshots, or to inspect one by id.

tools.name: eds_manage_snapshot
tools.description: Use this to add paths to a snapshot, remove them, publish it, submit a review decision, or delete it.
tools.unverified: Partly run against a live Edge Delivery Services site: the add and delete verbs were exercised as a reversible pair. The publish, review and remove verbs were not.

tools.name: eds_get_job_status
tools.description: Use this to check on a specific job by its site/ref/topic/name address, e.g. one returned earlier by eds_set_live_state or eds_reindex.

servers.description: Adobe Commerce Optimizer (ACO) admin and Merchandising API client — CLI and MCP server.

env.name: ACO_ADMIN_BASE_URL
env.description: Base URL of this tenant's ACO admin API. Resolved on the first tool call; without it every aco_* tool fails with a configuration error, not a credential error.

env.name: ACO_MERCHANDISING_BASE_URL
env.description: Base URL of this tenant's ACO Merchandising API. Required on exactly the same terms as ACO_ADMIN_BASE_URL — the server checks both together.

env.name: ACO_TOKEN
env.description: An admin Bearer pasted from a Studio session. One of two ways to obtain a credential — the other is minting from ACO_CLIENT_ID/ACO_CLIENT_SECRET — and it may also come from the credential file written by `hiberus-aco auth token set`.

env.name: ACO_CLIENT_ID
env.description: IMS client id. With ACO_CLIENT_SECRET it mints an admin Bearer, which is the alternative to supplying ACO_TOKEN; the credential-free catalog-search tools need neither.

env.name: ACO_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: IMS client secret. Only meaningful together with ACO_CLIENT_ID; the two are checked as a pair.

env.name: ACO_API_KEY
env.description: Sent as the `x-api-key` header on admin requests when set, omitted when not. Whether a tenant needs it is unconfirmed (aco design.md, Open Questions).

env.name: ACO_IMS_ORG_ID
env.description: Sent as the `x-gw-ims-org-id` header on admin requests when set, omitted when not. Same unconfirmed status as ACO_API_KEY.

tools.name: aco_search_catalog
tools.description: Use this to search a catalog view's products by phrase and page through results, with facet buckets included. No credential is required for an unprotected view.

tools.name: aco_get_facet_values
tools.description: Use this to check whether an attribute is facetable for a catalog view and list its available values with counts. No credential is required for an unprotected view.

tools.name: aco_list_catalog_views
tools.description: Use this to discover the catalog views (viewId, locales, default price book, policies) available in this tenant. Requires an ACO admin credential.

tools.name: aco_list_price_books
tools.description: Use this to list price books, optionally filtered by searchTerm, and to page through more with the returned scrollId. Requires an ACO admin credential.

tools.name: aco_list_policies
tools.description: Use this to list every policy configured in this tenant with its actions and filters, before deciding which filter to enable or disable. Requires an ACO admin credential.

tools.name: aco_toggle_policy_filter
tools.description: Use this to enable or disable one filter inside one named policy, addressed by the attribute it carries. There is no policy-level enable/disable in this API and no "apply to all" mode. Requires an ACO admin credential.

servers.description: Magento Cloud CLI wrapper — CLI and MCP server for read-only Magento Cloud project, environment, and database operations.

env.name: MAGENTO_CLOUD_CLI_TOKEN
env.description: An API token passed through to the magento-cloud CLI. Optional: a missing token is caught and the CLI's own stored session is used instead, so the server requires no environment variable at all.

tools.name: magentocloud_auth_status
tools.description: Use this to check whether the Magento Cloud CLI is authenticated before calling any other magentocloud_* tool. Never requires a credential itself.

tools.name: magentocloud_list_projects
tools.description: Use this to list every project accessible to the authenticated account — the starting point for finding a projectId.

tools.name: magentocloud_describe_project
tools.description: Use this to get one project's title and region by projectId, before listing its environments.

tools.name: magentocloud_list_environments
tools.description: Use this to list a project's environments (id, status, type, title) — most other tools need an environmentId as input.

tools.name: magentocloud_describe_environment
tools.description: Use this to get one environment's status and type by projectId/environmentId.

tools.name: magentocloud_get_environment_config
tools.description: Use this to fetch environment configuration facets on demand: variables, routes, services, serviceEndpoints (credentials never returned), appConfig, and urls.

tools.name: magentocloud_get_activities
tools.description: Use this to list recent deployment/activity events for a project, narrowed by limit, type, state or result — or to fetch one activity by activityId. Each event carries its machine-readable type and timings, never the human-readable description.

tools.name: magentocloud_get_activity_log
tools.description: Use this to read one activity's full deployment/build log by activityId, as plain text.

tools.name: magentocloud_query_database
tools.description: Use this for a bounded, read-only diagnostic query against an environment's database — a size check, or a single guarded SELECT/SHOW/DESCRIBE/EXPLAIN statement.

servers.description: Magento 2 REST API client — CLI and MCP server for catalog, orders, customers, stock and content, with opt-in write tools.

tools.name: magentorest_get_product_by_sku
tools.description: Use this to read one product by its SKU: name, price, status, visibility, type, timestamps, catalog attributes and category links.

tools.name: magentorest_search_products
tools.description: Use this to find products whose name contains a phrase. Returns a bounded page of summaries (id, sku, name, price, status, type) and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_advanced_product_search
tools.description: Use this to filter products on one field with a chosen comparison (eq, like, gt, gteq, lt, lteq, in, ...) and sort the result. Returns a bounded page of summaries and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_create_product
tools.description: Use this to create a new product. Adds a catalog record; the SKU must be unique. Does not touch stock or categories.

tools.name: magentorest_update_product
tools.description: Use this to change fields of an existing product. Only the fields you pass are sent; at least one is required. Overwrites the current values.

tools.name: magentorest_update_product_attribute
tools.description: Use this to set ONE attribute of a product by code (name, price, status, description, a custom attribute, ...). Overwrites the current value. The identity attributes sku, id, entity_id and type_id are refused.

tools.name: magentorest_delete_product
tools.description: Use this to permanently delete a product by SKU. Irreversible: the product, its images and its URL rewrites are removed.

tools.name: magentorest_assign_product_to_category
tools.description: Use this to add a product to a category at a position. Adds a link; it does not move the product out of other categories.

tools.name: magentorest_remove_product_from_category
tools.description: Use this to remove a product from one category. The product itself and its other category links are kept.

tools.name: magentorest_get_store_configs
tools.description: Use this to read each store view's configuration: code, locale, base currency, timezone, weight unit and base URLs.

tools.name: magentorest_get_store_views
tools.description: Use this to list every store view with its code, name, website, store group and whether it is active.

tools.name: magentorest_get_websites
tools.description: Use this to list every website with its code, name and default store group.

tools.name: magentorest_get_store_groups
tools.description: Use this to list every store group with its website, root category and default store view.

tools.name: magentorest_get_countries
tools.description: Use this to list the countries Magento knows, with ISO codes, English names and their regions.

tools.name: magentorest_get_currency_info
tools.description: Use this to read the base and display currency, the available currency codes and the exchange rates.

tools.name: magentorest_get_category_tree
tools.description: Use this to read the category structure under a root category as a flat list: each node has its id, parent_id, name, level, position, product count and whether it is active. Capped at 500 nodes; truncated says when the cap cut it short.

tools.name: magentorest_get_category_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one category by its numeric ID: name, parent, level, position, product count, children, URL path and catalog attributes.

tools.name: magentorest_list_categories
tools.description: Use this to find categories, optionally by parent, by a phrase in the name, or by active status. Returns a bounded page and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_get_products_in_category
tools.description: Use this to list the products assigned to one category. Returns a bounded page of product summaries (id, sku, name, price, status, type) and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_create_category
tools.description: Use this to create a category under a parent. Adds a record; it does not assign any product to it.

tools.name: magentorest_update_category
tools.description: Use this to change fields of an existing category. Only the fields you pass are sent; at least one is required. Overwrites the current values.

tools.name: magentorest_delete_category
tools.description: Use this to permanently delete a category and its subcategories by ID. Irreversible; the products stay in the catalog but lose the assignment.

tools.name: magentorest_move_category
tools.description: Use this to move a category under a different parent, optionally right after a sibling. Changes the category tree and the URL paths below it.

tools.name: magentorest_get_customer_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one customer by numeric ID: name, email, group, website, store and the default address IDs. Date of birth, tax number and the address book are not returned.

tools.name: magentorest_search_customers
tools.description: Use this to find customers by part of the email or name, by group or website, or by creation date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Filters are combined with AND. Returns a bounded page of summaries and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_get_customer_groups
tools.description: Use this to list the customer groups with their code and tax class.

tools.name: magentorest_get_customer_addresses
tools.description: Use this to list a customer's addresses by location: country, region, city, postcode and which is the default billing or shipping address. Street, telephone and the addressee are not returned.

tools.name: magentorest_create_customer
tools.description: Use this to create a customer account from an email and a name. It takes no password: Magento's own password-reset flow is how the customer sets one. Adds a record; the email must not already exist on the website.

tools.name: magentorest_update_customer
tools.description: Use this to change a customer's email, name or group. Only the fields you pass change; at least one is required. Overwrites the current values.

tools.name: magentorest_delete_customer
tools.description: Use this to permanently delete a customer account by ID. Irreversible: the account and its address book are removed; past orders keep their own copy of the details.

tools.name: magentorest_get_order_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one order by entity ID: status, state, totals, currency, the customer as the order records it, and the order lines. Billing and shipping addresses and payment details are not returned.

tools.name: magentorest_get_order_by_increment_id
tools.description: Use this to read one order by its order number (increment ID), the one a customer quotes. Same fields as reading by entity ID. A number with no order is reported as not-found.

tools.name: magentorest_search_orders
tools.description: Use this to find orders by status, customer email or ID, creation date range (YYYY-MM-DD, whole days) and grand-total range. Filters are combined with AND. Newest first unless you sort otherwise. Returns a bounded page of summaries and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_get_order_items
tools.description: Use this to list the lines of one order: SKU, name, quantities ordered, shipped, invoiced and refunded, price and row total, tax and discount.

tools.name: magentorest_get_order_comments
tools.description: Use this to read an order's status history: each entry's status, comment text, date and whether the customer was notified or can see it.

tools.name: magentorest_add_order_comment
tools.description: Use this to add a comment to an order's history, optionally moving it to another status. Silent and hidden from the customer unless you say otherwise: setting is_customer_notified to true makes Magento EMAIL the customer.

tools.name: magentorest_cancel_order
tools.description: Use this to cancel an order that has not been invoiced. Changes its state to canceled and releases the reserved stock; it cannot be undone from here.

tools.name: magentorest_hold_order
tools.description: Use this to put an order on hold, which stops it being invoiced or shipped until it is released with magentorest_unhold_order.

tools.name: magentorest_unhold_order
tools.description: Use this to release an order from hold so it can be invoiced and shipped again.

tools.name: magentorest_get_invoice_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one invoice by its numeric ID: state, totals, currency and the invoiced lines.

tools.name: magentorest_search_invoices
tools.description: Use this to find invoices by order, state and creation date range (YYYY-MM-DD, whole days). Filters are combined with AND. Returns a bounded page of summaries and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_get_shipment_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one shipment by its numeric ID: quantities, weight, the shipped lines and the tracking entries.

tools.name: magentorest_search_shipments
tools.description: Use this to find shipments by order and creation date range (YYYY-MM-DD, whole days). Filters are combined with AND. Returns a bounded page of summaries and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_get_creditmemo_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one credit memo (refund) by its numeric ID: state, totals, adjustments, currency and the refunded lines.

tools.name: magentorest_search_creditmemos
tools.description: Use this to find credit memos (refunds) by order, state and creation date range (YYYY-MM-DD, whole days). Filters are combined with AND. Returns a bounded page of summaries and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_create_invoice
tools.description: Use this to invoice an order, whole or by line. With capture set to true Magento CAPTURES the payment — the customer is charged; the default is false, which only records the invoice. Setting notify_customer to true emails the customer. Returns the new invoice ID.

tools.name: magentorest_create_shipment
tools.description: Use this to record a shipment for an order, whole or by line, optionally with tracking numbers. Setting notify_customer to true emails the customer. Returns the new shipment ID. Shipping deducts stock from the product's source: if a product has none there, Magento answers only "Could not save a shipment" (its log says the quantity is not available), so check stock first with magentorest_get_source_items.

tools.name: magentorest_add_shipment_tracking
tools.description: Use this to add a tracking number to an existing shipment. Adds an entry; it does not change the shipment's lines or notify the customer.

tools.name: magentorest_create_creditmemo
tools.description: Use this to REFUND an order, whole or by line, with optional shipping and manual adjustments. Money goes back to the customer; it cannot be undone from here. Setting notify_customer to true emails the customer. Returns the new credit memo ID.

tools.name: magentorest_get_product_stock
tools.description: Use this to read the stock item of one product by SKU: quantity, in-stock flag, whether stock is managed, sale quantity limits and backorder setting. With multi-source inventory enabled (the usual setup now) this legacy stock item mirrors only the default source, so it can show a null or zero quantity for a product held in other sources: use magentorest_get_source_items for every source.

tools.name: magentorest_get_low_stock_products
tools.description: Use this to list stock items at or below a quantity threshold, for one stock scope. Items already at zero are included. Returns a bounded page and the total count. With multi-source inventory enabled (the usual setup now) this legacy stock item mirrors only the default source, so it can show a null or zero quantity for a product held in other sources: use magentorest_get_source_items for every source.

tools.name: magentorest_get_inventory_sources
tools.description: Use this to list the inventory sources (warehouses) of multi-source inventory: code, name, whether enabled, country, region, city, postcode and priority. Street, phone, email and contact person are not returned.

tools.name: magentorest_get_inventory_stocks
tools.description: Use this to list the inventory stocks of multi-source inventory with the sales channels (websites) each one serves.

tools.name: magentorest_get_source_items
tools.description: Use this to read a product's quantity and status in each inventory source, by SKU.

tools.name: magentorest_update_product_stock
tools.description: Use this to set a product's stock quantity on the default stock. The in-stock flag follows the quantity (in stock when above zero) unless you set it. Overwrites the current quantity. With multi-source inventory enabled this changes the quantity of the default source (observed on a live store) and no other source; magentorest_get_source_items reads every source, and nothing here writes the others.

tools.name: magentorest_get_cart_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one cart by ID: activity, item count and quantity, currency, the customer's identity (id, name, email, group) and the cart lines. Addresses are not returned.

tools.name: magentorest_search_carts
tools.description: Use this to find carts by customer email or ID, active status and creation date range (YYYY-MM-DD, whole days). Filters are combined with AND. Returns a bounded page of summaries and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_get_cart_items
tools.description: Use this to list the lines of one cart: SKU, name, quantity, price and product type.

tools.name: magentorest_get_abandoned_carts
tools.description: Use this to find abandoned carts: active, non-empty carts not updated for at least a number of days, most recently updated first. Each entry names the owner (or Guest), the item count and the dates. Returns a bounded page, the total count and the cutoff used.

tools.name: magentorest_get_cms_block_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one CMS block by ID, including its content (HTML), title, identifier, dates and whether it is active.

tools.name: magentorest_search_cms_blocks
tools.description: Use this to find CMS blocks by identifier (exact), part of the title, or active status. Filters are combined with AND. Returns a bounded page of summaries WITHOUT the content, and the total count; read one by ID for its content.

tools.name: magentorest_update_cms_block
tools.description: Use this to change a CMS block's identifier, title, content or active flag. Only the fields you pass change; at least one is required. Overwrites the current values on the live storefront.

tools.name: magentorest_delete_cms_block
tools.description: Use this to permanently delete a CMS block by ID. Irreversible: it disappears from the storefront immediately.

tools.name: magentorest_get_cms_page_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one CMS page by ID, including its content (HTML), title, identifier, dates and whether it is active.

tools.name: magentorest_search_cms_pages
tools.description: Use this to find CMS pages by identifier (exact), part of the title, or active status. Filters are combined with AND. Returns a bounded page of summaries WITHOUT the content, and the total count; read one by ID for its content.

tools.name: magentorest_update_cms_page
tools.description: Use this to change a CMS page's identifier, title, content or active flag. Only the fields you pass change; at least one is required. Overwrites the current values on the live storefront.

tools.name: magentorest_delete_cms_page
tools.description: Use this to permanently delete a CMS page by ID. Irreversible: it disappears from the storefront immediately.

tools.name: magentorest_create_cms_block
tools.description: Use this to create a CMS block. Adds a block for all store views (Magento's REST body takes no store assignment) that is active unless you say otherwise.

tools.name: magentorest_create_cms_page
tools.description: Use this to create a CMS page at a URL key. Adds a page for all store views (Magento's REST body takes no store assignment) that is active, with a one-column layout, unless you say otherwise.

tools.name: magentorest_get_product_attribute
tools.description: Use this to read one product attribute by code: its input type, scope, flags (required, searchable, filterable, comparable), options and store labels.

tools.name: magentorest_search_product_attributes
tools.description: Use this to find product attributes by part of the code, input type (text, select, multiselect, boolean, ...), or the searchable and filterable flags. Filters are combined with AND. Returns a bounded page of summaries and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_get_attribute_options
tools.description: Use this to list the options of a select or multiselect attribute as label and value pairs.

tools.name: magentorest_get_attribute_sets
tools.description: Use this to list the product attribute sets with their ID, name and sort order. Returns a bounded page and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_get_attribute_set_attributes
tools.description: Use this to list the attributes that belong to one attribute set, as summaries (code, input type, label, required, searchable, filterable).

tools.name: magentorest_add_attribute_option
tools.description: Use this to add an option to a select or multiselect attribute. Adds an option that is not the default; it does not assign it to any product.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_get_product_media
tools.description: Use this to list a product's media entries (images and videos): ID, type, label, position, whether hidden, the roles it plays and its file path.

tools.name: magentorest_get_product_media_entry
tools.description: Use this to read one media entry of a product by its entry ID.

tools.name: magentorest_add_product_image
tools.description: Use this to add an image to a product from base64 data (at most 2,000,000 characters, JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP). Adds a media entry; it does not remove existing ones. Returns the new entry ID.

tools.name: magentorest_update_product_media
tools.description: Use this to change a media entry's label, position, roles or hidden flag. Only the fields you pass change; at least one is required. Overwrites the current values.

tools.name: magentorest_delete_product_media
tools.description: Use this to permanently delete one media entry of a product. Irreversible: the image stops showing on the storefront.

tools.name: magentorest_get_sales_rules
tools.description: Use this to list the cart price rules (promotions): name, dates, whether active, discount type and amount, coupon type, usage limits, websites and customer groups. Returns a bounded page and the total count.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_get_sales_rule_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one cart price rule by ID: its dates, discount, coupon type, usage limits, websites and customer groups.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_search_coupons
tools.description: Use this to find coupons by part of the code and by the rule they belong to. Filters are combined with AND. Returns a bounded page and the total count; each coupon shows its code, limits, times used and expiry.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_get_coupon_by_id
tools.description: Use this to read one coupon by ID: its code, rule, limits, times used and expiry.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_delete_coupon
tools.description: Use this to permanently delete one coupon by ID. Irreversible: customers holding that code can no longer redeem it.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_get_tax_rates
tools.description: Use this to list the tax rates: code, rate, country, region and postcode (or postcode range). Returns a bounded page and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_get_tax_rules
tools.description: Use this to list the tax rules: code, priority, and the customer tax classes, product tax classes and tax rates each one combines. Returns a bounded page and the total count.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_get_tax_classes
tools.description: Use this to list the tax classes, optionally only the CUSTOMER or only the PRODUCT ones. Returns one page of up to 100 and the total count.

tools.name: magentorest_get_revenue
tools.description: Use this to total the revenue of a period: revenue, currency, order count, average order value and tax. Computed from the orders in the period; it returns no order details. Reads at most max_pages pages of 100 orders and says when the result is partial.

tools.name: magentorest_get_order_count
tools.description: Use this to count the orders of a period, optionally by status. The count is Magento's own total, so it is exact and is never partial.

tools.name: magentorest_get_product_sales
tools.description: Use this to see what sold in a period: orders, items, units, revenue, and the ten best-selling products by quantity with their revenue. Optionally for one country (billing or shipping). Computed from the orders; it returns no order details. Reads at most max_pages pages of 100 orders and says when the result is partial.

tools.name: magentorest_get_revenue_by_country
tools.description: Use this to total the revenue of a period for one country (orders billed or shipped there): revenue, currency, order count, average order value and tax. Computed from the orders; it returns no order details. Reads at most max_pages pages of 100 orders and says when the result is partial.

tools.name: magentorest_get_customer_ordered_products_by_email
tools.description: Use this to list every order of one customer, found by exact email, with each order's lines (SKU, name, price, quantity). Returns the customer's id, name and email, never their addresses. For a product's own detail use magentorest_get_product_by_sku. Reads at most max_pages pages of 100 orders and says when the result is partial.

tools.name: magentorest_db_status
tools.description: Use this to check that the database connection works: returns the server version, the database name, that the session is read-only, and whether database writes are enabled. Run it first when a database tool fails.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_db_list_tables
tools.description: Use this to list the tables of the Magento database, optionally only those whose name contains a fragment (e.g. `sales_order`). Returns each table's name, engine and approximate row count (an estimate, not a count: use magentorest_db_stats or a COUNT(*) for exact figures).
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_db_describe_table
tools.description: Use this to see the columns of one table: name, type, whether it can be NULL, key, default and extra. Refuses the tables that hold credentials (administrators, OAuth tokens, integrations).
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_db_query
tools.description: Use this for a question the other tools cannot answer: runs ONE read-only SELECT and returns its columns and rows. Name the columns (SELECT * is refused; COUNT(*) is fine), pass values as ? placeholders in params, and expect at most max_rows rows (default 100, at most 500; a LIMIT above that is refused, none is added for you). No comments, no second statement, no INTO, no locking, and no credential tables (administrators, OAuth tokens, integrations); values of columns named like a password, hash or token, and of secret configuration rows, come back as [redacted].
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_db_magento_tables
tools.description: Use this to see the well-known Magento 2 tables grouped by what they hold (products, categories, customers, orders, quotes, invoices, shipments, CMS, EAV, URL rewrites, store), each marked with whether it exists in this database. Table prefixes are not applied.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_db_product_by_sku
tools.description: Use this for a quick look at one product straight from the database: id, SKU, type, created and updated dates, quantity and in-stock flag (legacy stock table). For the full product use magentorest_get_product_by_sku.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_db_recent_orders
tools.description: Use this to see the latest orders straight from the database: id, increment id, status, state, customer email and name, totals, currency and dates. Newest first; limit defaults to 10, at most 100. Never returns addresses or payment data.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_db_stats
tools.description: Use this to count the rows of the key tables in one call: products, categories, customers, orders, order items, quotes, CMS pages and blocks. A table that does not exist says so.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

tools.name: magentorest_db_execute
tools.description: Use this ONLY when no other tool can make the change: runs ONE INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE (UPDATE and DELETE need a WHERE) in a transaction. It bypasses Magento's own validation, indexing and events, so a change made here may not show on the storefront until a reindex and cache flush. Try it first with dry_run=true: the statement runs and is rolled back, and you see how many rows it would change. It rolls back by itself, changing nothing, if more than max_affected rows (default 100, at most 10000) would change. No DDL (DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE), no REPLACE, no comments, no credential tables. Irreversible once committed.
tools.unverified: this tool has not been run against a real Magento instance; its request shape and response projection are covered by unit tests against a test double and by the conformance suite.

env.name: MAGENTO_REST_BASE_URL
env.description: The Magento REST root every magentorest_* tool addresses, e.g. https://<host>/rest/V1 (or /rest/<store-code>/V1 for one store view). Resolved on the first tool call and refused without it; tools/list still works. Must be https — plain http is accepted only for localhost.

env.name: MAGENTO_REST_TOKEN
env.description: A Magento integration access token or admin token, sent as a Bearer. Every tool call needs one, but it may come from this variable OR from the credential file written by `hiberus-magento-rest auth token set`, so neither source is required on its own.

env.name: MAGENTO_REST_FIELDS_FILE
env.description: Path to a JSON file that ADDS fields to what a resource exposes, e.g. {"product":{"add":["cost"]}}. Additive only — a resource may carry only `add`, so a file can widen the shipped list but never narrow or replace it — and credential and payment fields (passwords, hashes, tokens, secrets, card and payment data) can never be added. Read once at startup; a file that cannot be read or does not validate stops the server with exit code 1 rather than starting with a half-applied configuration.

env.name: MAGENTO_REST_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Set to exactly `true` to register the write tools (create, update, delete, cancel, invoice, refund, ...). Unset, or any other value, and the server registers read tools only — a write tool is then absent from tools/list, not merely refused. Read once at startup.

env.name: MAGENTO_REST_GROUPS
env.description: Comma-separated tool groups to load, e.g. `products,customers`, so a project registers only the tools it needs instead of every one. Groups: `products`, `store`, `categories`, `customers`, `orders`, `sales-documents`, `stock`, `carts`, `cms`, `attributes`, `media`, `promotions`, `tax`, `analytics`, `database` (only with MAGENTO_REST_DATABASE_CONNECTION; naming it without one stops the server). Case-insensitive; blanks and repeats are ignored. Unset or empty loads every group (`database` too, when a connection is configured). A name that is not a group stops the server with exit code 1, listing the valid ones. MAGENTO_REST_ALLOW_WRITES still decides whether the write tools of a loaded group are registered. Read once at startup.

env.name: MAGENTO_REST_DATABASE_CONNECTION
env.description: Adds the `database` tool group (magentorest_db_*): direct, read-only access to the Magento database. A URL with NO password, e.g. `mysql://reader@127.0.0.1:3306/magento`; a password in it stops the server. A host that is not this machine uses verified TLS unless you write `?ssl=false`. Unset, there are no database tools. Use a database user with the narrowest grants you can: SELECT only unless you also enable writes. The URL is validated at startup (exit code 1 if it is invalid); the password is only needed when a tool is called.

env.name: MAGENTO_REST_DATABASE_PASSWORD
env.description: The password of the database user, used by the database tools. It may come from this variable OR from the credential file written by `hiberus-magento-rest auth db-password set` (read from stdin, mode 0600), so neither source is required on its own. Resolved on every connection, so a stored password applies without a restart.

env.name: MAGENTO_REST_DATABASE_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Set to exactly `true` to register magentorest_db_execute (one INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE per call, in a transaction, with a dry run and a cap on rows changed). A switch of its own: MAGENTO_REST_ALLOW_WRITES does not enable it. Unset, or any other value, and the tool is absent from tools/list. Without MAGENTO_REST_DATABASE_CONNECTION it stops the server with exit code 1. Read once at startup.
